recipes.name: Deluxe Corned Beef Hash
ingredients_raw: 5 large Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch cubes
0.5 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Melt butter with olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion until lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in potatoes and carrot; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 15 minutes.
Stir in corned beef, parsley, pepper, thyme, and salt. Cook, stirring often, until hash is crisp and browned, 10 to 15 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Deluxe Corned Beef Hash
raw_recipe.description: This corned beef hash combines cooked corned beef with crispy potatoes and onions for a delicious way to use up leftover St. Paddy's Day corned beef.

video.description: For a filling breakfast or brunch, look no further than this Corned beef and potato hash - featuring Idaho Yukon Gold Potatoes. Perfect for Saint Patrick's day leftovers.

review.reviewBody: Props to the recipe submitter for using homemade corned beef (not out of a can, like the 2 top rated recipes on the site). I think, as written, this recipe is a solid 4 stars, and I did try to follow closely, but the end result seemed to be missing something. I used leftover corned beef from the recipe Slow Cooked Corned Beef for Sandwiches. I did omit the olive oil, and instead just used 2 tablespoons of salted butter. I also omitted the carrots. I had cooked the potatoes the night before, so I diced them up and added them to the onions while they were cooking. In addition to the recommended ingredients, I added 1 teaspoon of garlic powder and 2 tsp of Worcestershire sauce. I also used quite a bit of fresh cracked black pepper (I didn't want it spicy, I just wanted it to have a nice bold flavor). I then pressed it in to the pan and let it cook on medium low to get just a little bit of a crisp on it. Served it with an egg and toasted rye bread, and it was absolutely killer.

I made a mash up of this recipe and Chef John’s recipe for corned beef hash. I followed this recipe for the most part, but omitted the carrots and added a red bell pepper and a few cloves of garlic, as well as four stalks of chopped green onions. I also seasoned it with some garlic salt. Mine took quite a bit longer to get the crust, but it was well worth it. It crisped up very nicely and I added a poached egg on top!

This is a family favorite. Like others commented making homemade hash requires a fresh made corned beef not canned. I boil my corned beef with a stout beer the night before and then use a food processor. I omit the carrots and the butter. I sauté my onions in olive oil. What makes this recipe is the thyme. Best recipe for real corned beef hash!

We will be making this each time we have leftover corned beef. We used the uncured corned beef from Fresh Thyme and it was so tender and delicious. I cooked onions until translucent before adding potatoes and then covered them for the first five mins to let them cook through a little better. I also added a splash of Worcestershire sauce and a sprinkle of garlic powder towards the end. A lot less work than cooking the potatoes ahead of time...just took longer and less cleanup this way.

I used canned corned beef because it is out of season. I only added a pinch of salt. For speed, I used frozen diced hash browns and about 1/4 -1/3 cup beef stock. Turned out nearly undetectable as canned meat. Great results!

I boiled the potatoes ahead of time and did not add the carrots. Also used Wigley's Corned Beef only available in the Detroit, Michigan area. Very tender and well seasoned. I added a couple of eggs at the end. My husband loved it!

I used boarhead corned beef from the deli, and I put all ingredients (separately) in my food processor, which definitely saved on time. It was good, my family liked it and I would consider making it again, with a little less peper. Also I read somewhere if you put two tablespoons of heavy cream in it, it will give it a nice brown crisp bottom, which did seem to work.
Really enjoyed it. Added more vegtables when grilling potatoes--diced mushrooms, peppers, and onoins. Yummy. Also floated some poached eggs on top. Yummy.

I made this for breakfast this morning as my husband and I are big fans of corned beef. ( not the canned stuff) I had made corned beef in the slow cooker yesterday and this was the perfect way to use leftovers. Followed recipe mostly, but added yellow bell pepper instead of the carrot. Also added garlic to the seasoning. Will definitely make this one again!

Excellent recipe. I would definitely make it again. I’d like to know how much potatoes you use in weight. Also, I think that the amount of corn beef was a little too much in proportion to the rest of the recipe would reduce it to a pound. Thanks for sharing this great recipe. Pam.
I love my veggies, so I added some fresh baby spinach, peas, and diced parboiled sweet potato to the mix. Topped with a fried egg and a side of pumpernickel toast, it was a hit!

I have six cans of New Zealand corned beef to use up so I searched for recipes with corned beef. This seems like a breakfast/brunch meal, but I made it for dinner, complete with the egg on top. It was super easy to make. My husband loved it and we both ate it again the next night and for lunch.
Well as compared to other reviews the only chg I made is I DID include the carrots. It added moisture without added grease. Very good recipe. Wouldn’t change a thing.
I added some leftover mustard sauce. Took it to the next level!!
Added a little garlic Very nice

My first time making a corned beef hash. Someone gifted me a corned beef so used the left overs to make this. Was easy to make and it tasted good. Might add more seasoning next go around. But good as is.
Good, wanted to try hash, but we prefer our leftover corned beef in Reuben sandwiches.

With leftover corned beef and cabbage and potatoes, I wanted a “reminder” recipe to make some breakfast hash. (I would not have thought of thyme, so thank you!) I made as shown (but a half recipe), but used some leftover boiled potato,cubed, as well as raw - that worked just fine. My only “change” was that I did add a couple shakes of smoked paprika, which I think added to the flavor. Thank you, this is a solid recipe!
Must have Worcestershire to add some zip. Otherwise a very good basic recipe.
